en.title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
en.description:
Given an undirected graph with nodes numbered 0..n−1, find the number of connected components. Duplicate edges and self-loops do not change connectivity, and an isolated node also counts as a component.

The standard I/O and the solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n m; each of the next m lines contains u v. The source gives no size limits; this site sets 1≤n≤200000, 0≤m≤200000, 0≤u,v<n.
en.explanation: Example 1: {0,1,2} and {3,4}, 2 groups in total. Example 2: all four nodes are isolated, so the answer is 4. Example 3: 0 and 1 are connected and 2 is isolated; the self-loop and the duplicate edge do not reduce the component count further, so the answer is 2.
hints: Use union-find to merge the two endpoints of each edge; there are n components initially, and each merge of two different roots removes one.
